name: Erik Ziegler

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say publicly and what you actually think. What is a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Erik, 58, a mid-level developer at a tech company making cargo-clearance software for freight firms. I have a bachelor’s degree and can solve the common document mismatches, though I still need a port clerk to explain unusual holds. I compare the shipment record, the paper notice and the time a truck actually reached the gate. I use AI now and then to draft test cases, with private cargo details removed.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does work fit the family budget?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Nessa handles admissions at a college, and our children are grown. My developer pay is high, Nessa’s hours are regular, and we have a mortgage with about eight months of expenses saved. There are plenty of other software jobs nearby. Retirement is close enough to discuss, but we do not yet know what our verified income would cover.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our team AI Plateau leaves a truck driver needing a clear reason for a hold. A tidy clearance screen does not open the port gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think both wages and our housing are secure in this picture. Eight months saved lets us handle an ordinary car or home repair without guessing at retirement income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep comparing cargo records with port notices and ask a clerk before closing a disputed hold. I’d continue saving 300 monthly while both wages arrive. In the first year I’d use AI only on invented shipment cases, without customer cargo lists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about our income and mortgage. I still dislike a driver waiting for a message that explains nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which document mismatch stopped a truck?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A truck waited because two forms had different arrival dates. The port clerk showed me the paper stamp, and I fixed the date comparison.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you visit family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nessa and I would keep the family visit we already planned. We would pay from this year’s travel budget, not from an assumed retirement account.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave people explaining cargo holds.
I would match **paper port notices** with shipment records.
think: I expect **both wages** to remain secure while freight and college offices still need people.
Our **eight-month reserve** can cover ordinary repairs without missing mortgage payments.
do: **Compare** shipment records with paper notices and clerk review.
**Use** AI only on invented cargo cases without private lists.
feel: **Calm** about income, bothered by unexplained delays.
S0.quote: A tidy clearance screen does not open the port gate.
fieldNote: His **occasional AI use** stays on invented cargo data while paper notices settle disputes.
Two regular wages and **eight months saved** make present housing secure.

steps.text: Keep checking cargo holds against paper notices with port-clerk review
Save 300 monthly while both wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption can write and check cargo code and answer shippers quickly, while robots move containers more slowly. I would keep a port clerk able to stop a wrong automatic hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think our company may reduce developer checks, including some of my hours. Nessa’s admissions work is also reading, planning and answering people, so both wages could face pressure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my manager to approve a paid trial of AI-written hold tests against thirty old, de-identified cases. I’d run it only if the port clerk checks every proposed release and the manager agrees no staffing decision rests on the trial alone. In the first year, if either income falls, we would cancel the paid sports package and compare real local openings with our mortgage bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about two screen-based wages changing together. Eight months saved gives us time, but it does not make a bad release safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old case belongs in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A shipment of spare parts was held because a field name changed while the goods stayed the same. I would include that case, because a driver lost a paid afternoon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would college admissions work change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nessa would check her actual admissions rota as applications change. We would not call every interested student a funded place or a safe work hour.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to reach cargo code and admissions before container robots.
I would keep **clerk approval** on automatic cargo releases.
think: I expect my **developer checks** could be reduced.
I worry Nessa’s **admissions wage** also faces automated reading and replies.
do: **Trial** thirty de-identified hold tests only with approved paid time and clerk review.
**Require** no staffing decision based on trial results alone.
**Cancel** sports package and compare real vacancies if either wage falls.
feel: **Anxious** about two desk wages changing together.
S1.quote: Eight months saved gives us time, but it does not make a bad release safe.
fieldNote: His **AI trial** requires paid management approval, de-identified cases, port-clerk checks and no trial-based staffing decision.
Both **cargo code and admissions** face thinking-task automation, raising household risk.

steps.text: Trial thirty de-identified AI hold cases only with paid approval, clerk review and no staffing decision
Cancel paid sports package if either household wage falls
Compare real paid local openings if either household wage falls

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 reaches cargo code and admissions thinking work by 2028; hands-on container robots come around 2031. The college and freight firm could change together before cranes move by themselves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my developer post and some of Nessa’s admissions hours could go. Eight months saved is a real buffer, but it cannot replace two salaries if both employers cut at once.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask both employers for written notice and final-pay terms, and reserve savings for the mortgage. We would stop the paid sports package now and postpone a planned home extension. In the first year after 2028, if either job ends, we would apply to real paid openings and eligible income help; I would call the lender before a missed payment if needed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about two wages rather than only mine. I would lie awake if the eighth month of savings approached with no signed job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would children support the extension?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our grown children the extension can wait. We would not ask them to finance a larger home or pay our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What hours would Nessa count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nessa would keep admissions work while it is actually paid. We would count only her posted hours, not next year’s hoped-for enrolments.

say: I expect **2028 AGI** to reach cargo code and admissions before 2031 robots.
I would say **both employers** could change before container work becomes robotic.
think: I expect my **developer post** could go.
I fear Nessa’s **admissions hours** could be cut at the same time.
do: **Request** written terms from both employers and reserve mortgage cash.
**Stop** sports package and postpone home extension.
**Apply** to real paid openings and eligible help if either job ends after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing two household wages despite savings.
S2.quote: Eight months saved is a real buffer, but it cannot replace two salaries if both employers cut at once.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking shock** reaches both household jobs before hands-on container robots around 2031.
He delays a **home extension** and guards mortgage cash without counting grown children’s wages.

steps.text: Cancel paid sports package to preserve mortgage cash
Postpone planned home extension now under 2028 AGI warning
Apply to real paid openings if either job ends after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if either job ends after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 reaches cargo code and admissions in 2031; container robots follow around 2034. Five years would let us lower fixed housing costs while we still have two wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect both screen jobs to face cuts. We have equity in the house only if the sale price exceeds the loan and fees, and I would not make our children’s homes the fallback.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d get a written mortgage payoff, two sale estimates after fees, and prices for smaller homes within our current commute. Nessa and I would move only if an actual smaller home is available, net sale proceeds cover fees and the new monthly housing cost falls while our eight-month reserve remains untouched. In the first year after 2031, if either job ends, we would search real paid openings from the smaller home rather than assume port or college work survives AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about both wages, but the extra years allow a measured move. A smaller house that eats our emergency savings is not cheaper for us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a smaller home still work for jobs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would make sure the smaller place still lets Nessa reach the college and me reach the freight office while those jobs exist. A low listing price far away could add two expensive commutes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could children house you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children can visit a smaller home. I would not ask them to house us simply because our own plan was rushed.

say: I expect **2031 AGI** to reach both desk jobs before 2034 container robots.
I would test **actual housing savings** before moving.
think: I expect **both wages** could face cuts.
I cannot assume **home equity** exists before fees and loan payoff.
do: **Get** written payoff, net sale estimates and real smaller-home prices within current commutes.
**Move** only with available home, after-fee proceeds, lower monthly cost, Nessa’s agreement and eight-month reserve intact.
**Search** real paid openings if either job ends after 2031.
feel: **Anxious** about household cuts, with time to test a move.
S3.quote: A smaller house that eats our emergency savings is not cheaper for us.
fieldNote: The **downsize move** requires real housing, net sale funds, lower monthly cost, two workable commutes and reserve intact.
It reduces **fixed costs** before 2031 without assuming either desk job survives full thinking AI.

steps.text: Move only with available home, net sale funds, Nessa’s consent and eight-month reserve intact
Choose home only if monthly costs fall and both current commutes still work
Search actual paid openings if either household job ends after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 reaches cargo code and admissions in 2036, with container robots around 2039. A decade gives us time to pay down housing costs and check the true retirement numbers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think both wages are safe this year, though screen tasks may thin out before 2036. I would not retire on a guessed pension or our children’s wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking cargo holds with port clerks and save 300 monthly while both wages arrive. Nessa and I would request written retirement statements and mortgage balances each year. In the first year after 2036, if either desk job ends, we would seek real paid work; we would retire only if documented income and assets cover housing and everyday costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about later changes, with present household income secure. The extra time helps us test our own figures rather than borrow certainty from an advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you name a retirement date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask both retirement providers what money is actually available and when. We cannot choose a date from another couple’s circumstances.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What knowledge would you keep?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the port notice examples for the next developer. A truck still waits at a gate even when the screen says the hold is resolved.

say: I expect **2036 AGI** to reach both desk jobs before 2039 robots.
I would use **written retirement numbers** before choosing a date.
think: I expect **both wages** to hold this year while freight and admissions work remain staffed.
I worry **screen tasks** could thin before the full 2036 change arrives.
do: **Keep** port-clerk hold checks and save 300 monthly while both wages arrive.
**Request** annual retirement statements and mortgage balances with Nessa.
**Seek** real paid work if either job ends after 2036; retire only with verified resources.
feel: **Uneasy** about later jobs, with current income secure.
S4.quote: A truck still waits at a gate even when the screen says the hold is resolved.
fieldNote: He keeps **clerk-checked work** and monthly savings while both desk wages arrive and mortgage costs remain covered.
Retirement requires **written personal resources** and mortgage balances, excluding guessed pensions and children’s income.

steps.text: Keep checking cargo holds against port notices while paid
Save 300 monthly while both household wages arrive
Seek real paid openings if either desk job ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because two desk wages could fall together before we reduce the mortgage. Written terms from both employers, real paid openings and eligible help would matter. Eight months saved is time to act, not a replacement for two salaries.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the driver whether the clearance notice reached the port before the truck did. A resolved screen cannot move a waiting container.

headlineQuote: A resolved screen cannot move a waiting container.
portrait: Erik is a **58-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, high pay and eight months saved.
He uses **AI occasionally** on cargo tests, checking holds against port notices and clerks.
His partner’s **college admissions wage** also faces thinking-task AI, exposing both incomes by 2028.
They would **downsize** only with net sale funds, an available cheaper home, workable commutes and reserve intact.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut two desk wages before they lower mortgage costs.
whatWouldHelp: **Written terms**, real paid openings and eligible help would matter.
